pose_matches: METHOD. Landmarks are source pixels on the 1086x1448 canvas: flower centre and brooch by flood-fill centroid (+-1 px), chin of the faceless busts from the face-black region (+-2 px), chins / eyes / mouths of faced images read from gridded 1:1 crops (+-10 px). Transforms are p' = s*p + t (scale s, offset t in source px) mapping image B onto image A; on screen, if A is drawn at k = dst.w/1086, draw B at scale k*s and shift it by k*t. Checked with onion-skin overlays in <scratchpad>\asset_comp\asset_reg_*.png.

THE THREE POSES ARE CONFIRMED: (A) faceless front bust = female -4 / 少年1 / 成年1 (+ 猫耳娘1); (B) head bowed looking down-left = female -3 / 少年2 / 成年2; (C) one hand reaching = female -2 / 少年3 / 成年3. Female -1 (square face close-up) has no partner. In every image the flower sits at viewer's right of the head and the head axis leans 22-31 deg the same way, so the flower is a reliable common anchor.

POSE A head sizes (flower centre to chin): f4 452 px, 猫耳娘1 451, 少年1 508, 成年1 518. So the male heads are drawn 12-15% larger than the female one and their chins sit ~97 px lower on the canvas (f4 chin y 628, 少年1 724, 成年1 727).

A1  猫耳娘1 -> f4: s 1.00, t (-28,-49). Residual chin 2 px, flower 4 px, brooch 6 px. It is the same drawing redone with ears (hair strands differ by a few px). Best match in the whole set: holds as a hard cut, a 2-3 frame dissolve, or an ear-only reveal.

A2  少年1 -> f4: s 0.89, t (+60,-18) (inverse f4 -> 少年1: s 1.123, t (-67,+21)). Residual chin 5 px, flower 5 px; brooch lands 24 px higher (shorter neck). After registration the boy's capelet at shoulder height is ~45 px narrower per side than her cape. Clean gender match cut: face void, flower and collar stay put, the long hair 'cuts short'. Unregistered they are 96 px apart at the chin: registration is required.
A3  成年1 -> f4: s 0.873, t (+81,-4). Residual 8 px at chin / flower, brooch 10 px. His shoulder line lands on her cape line (y ~820) but ~150 px wider per side.

A4  成年1 <-> 少年1: no transform needed (s 1.0, t 0): chin within 3 px, flower 29 px, brooch 22 px; silhouette IoU 0.87, head-box IoU 0.96. Hair outline nearly coincides; only capelet vs square jacket shoulders differ. (Least-squares refinement s 0.963, t (+36,+23) is not worth it.)
POSE B head sizes (flower to chin): f3 529, 少年2 526, 成年2 557.

B1  成年2 <-> 少年2: no transform (s 1.0, t 0): nose 16 px, chin 9 px, flower 26 px, brooch 39 px; silhouette IoU 0.89, head-box IoU 0.97. Direct swap works; the eyes change from half-open (boy) to closed (man).

B2  少年2 -> f3: s 1.00, t (-31,-43). Residual nose 15 px, chin 23 px, flower 33 px (rms 25), brooch misses by 75 px. WEAKEST of the three pose matches: f3 is a strict profile with no eye, the boy / man are three-quarter views with faces. Head mass, bow direction and flower line up well enough for a hard cut on a flash or a wipe; do not cross-dissolve. 成年2 -> f3: s 0.95, t (+2,-5), rms 30.

POSE C head sizes (flower to chin): f2 381, 少年3 437, 成年3 384. Reaching palm centres: f2 (290,1100), 少年3 (226,1140), 成年3 (212,1160); all three hands occupy the same lower-left zone (x ~30-460, y ~900-1380).

C1  成年3 <-> 少年3: no transform: hand within 24 px, brooch 28 px, flower 34 px; silhouette IoU 0.90 (torso, sleeves and offered hand are the same drawing). The HEADS do not match: the boy's is 14% larger and his chin is 68 px lower, both eyes open vs one. Lock on torso + hand and let the head change (reads as growing up / down). Face-locked alternative: 成年3 -> 少年3 s 1.084, t (-33,+2), but then the hand misses by ~120 px.

C2  少年3 -> f2: one transform for head and hand together: s 1.00, t (+65,-40): palm 1 px, chin 29 px, flower 28 px. (Face-only fit s 0.886, t (+110,+12) leaves the hand 80 px off.) The gesture itself differs: her hand is palm-out with spread fingers pointing down-left, his is palm-up with fingers to the right; her eyes are closed, his open. Works as a beat cut that keeps 'head top centre, hand bottom left'; not a morph.
C3  成年3 -> f2: s 1.00, t (+78,-10) (or s 0.935, t (+95,+21), rms 21 over chin / mouth / eye / flower / palm). Same caveats as C2.

RECOMMENDATION FOR THE GENDER LINE: use pose A. f_bust held -> hard cut on the keyword to boy_bust drawn at 0.89x with offset (+60,-18) -> optional third hit man_bust (0.873x, (+81,-4)) or straight back. Pose C (boy_reach) can then follow as the 'do whatever' image without needing registration because it enters on its own cut.

Ornament caveat for cuts: female -1 and -3 wear a rectangular-ray rosette (orange centre / black centre), every other image a pointed-petal daisy with a ring centre. A cut between f_profile and any pose-A / pose-C image changes the ornament shape; the code-drawn spark (12 petals, src/components/motif.js) sits between the two.
processing_needed: Bring the files into the project under ASCII keys (suggested: f_bust, f_profile, f_reach, f_eye, boy_bust, boy_down, boy_reach, man_bust, man_down, man_reach, cat_bust, cat_paws, cat_sleep) in assets/character/. The source names contain spaces and CJK ('ChatGPT 图像 2026年10月6日 01_31_06-4.png', '少年1.png'); export/server.mjs does decode URLs, but art keys are used in code and regions.json.
Normalise canvases: female -4 is 1086x1449 (crop the last row to 1448); female -1 is 1254x1254 and must be treated as its own format (square, different scale).

Clean the alpha once at load (or offline): set a<16 to 0. Every image has 80-230 detached specks and a faint haze at alpha 1-8 (1-2k px detached, ~20-29k px in all) whose RGB is saturated red / yellow. Invisible in normal compositing (worst pixel alpha 26), but any matte stacking, outline / dilate, threshold or glow built from the alpha would bring them out as red dots (they are exactly the red dots seen when a viewer ignores alpha). Optionally stretch 250-254 to 255: the solid body is alpha 253/254, never 255 (same quirk the old cut-outs had).

Add a three-ink treatment (suggested art.inks(ctx, name, dst, { orange: 'me', cream: 'text', black: 'panel', alpha })): at load classify each pixel to its nearest ink (soft at the anti-aliased boundaries) into three mattes, at draw time tint each matte with a palette role. This is what makes the new art obey the film's colour-as-state rule (off = greys, warm = hotter orange, error, ash) and lets one ink be dropped or swapped. The art is flat enough for it: 94-98% of opaque pixels lie within 24 levels of an ink, the rest are ink-to-ink blends, true stray colours are 0.01-0.12%.

Normalise the inks across images so cuts do not shift colour. Measured medians: orange #D26A39 to #E1703C (set median ~#DC723F), cream #F1DFC4 to #F7E4CB (~#F4E0C6), black #201713 to #2B1E19 (~#241A16). f_profile has the darkest orange, boy_reach the lightest black. With the ink remap this is automatic.
Handle the fourth tone in female -2 (f_reach): dark rust #432318 on 4.5% of the opaque area. Fold it into black or map it to meDim.

Solve black-on-dark. The black ink (#241A16) is almost exactly the UI page: on.bg #262624, error.bg #1d1413, ash.bg #1c1b1a. Size rule for flat art: at 4K a bust filling the 1080-high frame is 1.49x source (under the 1.75x warning in art.draw). The male set (and boy_bust most of all) has a 1 px grey-brown keyline on cream edges (rim #C3B5A3, up to -48 luminance). It is part of the look on dark; on cream / white fields it reads as a hairline. If the cream ink is remapped, the rim must be remapped with it (build the cream matte from alpha, not from colour distance alone).

Mirroring: every figure has the flower at viewer's right and poses B / C face or reach toward viewer's LEFT. Layouts that need the figure on the left reaching right (toward the user's side of the thread, which is on the right in this UI) must flip the image; this is safe for flat art (no lettering) but moves the flower to viewer's left, so decide once and keep it consistent.

Memory / load: the current _prepare keeps img + grey + inverted + silhouette at full resolution per image (~25 MB each). Thirteen more images plus three ink mattes each is several hundred MB; prepare lazily or drop the inverted plate for images only used through inks.

loading_pipeline:
HOW IT WORKS TODAY. config.json paths.art = "assets/character". src/engine/engine.js createEngine() (line 51) awaits loadArt(cfg) alongside fonts and the two copy JSONs, and passes the result to every section as env.art (line 61). src/engine/art.js: ART_NAMES (line 19) is a hard-coded list ['library','tea','rain','gaze','plea','parted']; loadArt() fetches /assets/character/<name>.png for each, decodes it and calls Art._prepare(), then fetches assets/character/regions.json (missing file = empty regions, no error). _prepare() builds per image, once: a 160x240 luminance + alpha map (for halftone / ascii), full-resolution greyscale, inverted-greyscale and white-silhouette canvases (for draw's desaturation, duotone, silhouette), and a 256x384 blurred colour + grey copy (for backdrop). Treatments: draw (crop, alpha, sat follows the palette's sat so art greys with the conversation state; warns in the console above 1.75x source at 4K), cover (crop rect for cover-fit with focus / zoom), silhouette (alpha matte in one palette role), duotone (luminance -> two palette roles, keeps the matte), halftone, ascii, slices, backdrop. Addressing: art.<treatment>(ctx, 'key', dstRect, opts); art.size('key'); art.region('key', 'face' | 'crops.bust' | 'crops.wide.0' ...) reads regions.json and returns {x,y,w,h} for arrays of 4 numbers or a box for [cx,cy,r]. regions.json holds, per image: alpha flag, face box, eyes_y, flower / brooch / emblem circles, hands, prop, figure (alpha bounds), crops (avatar, bust, wide[3], detail[]), notes. Rooms: room() in src/components/chat.js line 56 calls art.backdrop when given { art, name }; without a name it draws a soft lit page (so rooms work with no picture). client() in src/scenes/kit.js passes env.art through. tools/storyboard.mjs stubs art with a Proxy (line 18), so new art methods do not break the storyboard tool. Old art is used in 9 of 13 section files (not in 03_verse1, 04_pre1, 11_count); the keys also appear in docs/v3/errors.json attempts[].art.

WHAT ADDING THE NEW SET INVOLVES. (1) Copy the 10 silhouettes (and the 3 cat-ear files that already exist in 圖片\Claude猫耳娘) into assets/character under ASCII keys and extend ART_NAMES, or make the list data-driven from regions.json. (2) In _prepare(): alpha clean-up (a<16 -> 0), aspect-correct luminance / blur sizes (they assume 2:3; the new art is 3:4 and one 1:1), and three ink mattes per image for a new palette-driven treatment (art.inks). (3) regions.json entries for each new key from the measured landmarks in this report, plus hard-edge flags and the registration table for match cuts. (4) Re-derive every figure rect in the scenes (all are 2:3) and every crop that names an old region. (5) Decide what replaces the three scene illustrations: tea / rain / library currently give the rooms their colour (art.backdrop in ~25 shots) and are the 'pictures she sends' (c1-happy, left-away pane, out-study, exec-09). The new set contains no scene or background, so rooms become room() without art (or a code-drawn room / a blurred bust as a colour source) and the 'picture she sends' becomes a silhouette portrait card. (6) The old figure placements are full-body (head to boots); the new art is busts only, so the figure behind the glass, the figure inside the frame and the full-height exec figures need bust compositions (rising from the bottom edge of the window / frame, or framed as a card). (7) Update PLAN.md section 4, KIT.md, README.md, CREDITS.md, errors.json art fields. Existing treatments work on the new files as they are: silhouette (true alpha), halftone / ascii (luminance: black 0.11, orange 0.52, cream 0.89, so three clear tiers), duotone (gives a three-step ramp but cannot colour the inks independently), draw with sat (greys correctly).

Hand-only art: palm against the glass seen from the other side (WANTED_ART A4), typing hands or a finger pressing a button (B5) for the regenerate attempts.
Seated / waiting pose looking off-frame (A5), both arms giving or holding something out (B4), thinking pose (C1), seated asleep / powered-down pose (C2; cat_sleep is the nearest).

The flower ornament alone, front-on, high resolution (B3). It stays code-drawn; note the set itself shows two ornament designs (rectangular-ray rosette in female -1 / -3, pointed-petal daisy elsewhere).

Right-facing or mirrored variants: all poses face or reach toward viewer's left with the flower at viewer's right; the user's side of the thread is on the right, so reaching 'toward the user' needs a flip.

Landscape or wide compositions: everything is portrait 3:4 (one 1:1), at most ~810 virtual px wide at full frame height; and resolution is 1448 px on the long side, below the 2048 px asked for in WANTED_ART (a head close-up at 4K is ~3.6x source).
